fix(cpp): enforce the central input limits at every library boundary of the native gateway

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-combine-1-20261119-44443689630-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi. This branch contains ONLY the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`: runtime layer `include/uos/rt` + `src/rt`, application under `src/`, vendored libraries under `third_party/`, 451 test binaries green on Linux ARM64 in release and under sanitizers) plus `static/` web assets. The original TypeScript gateway it was ported from is no longer in this branch; it lives on branch `development` (which is what production runs today) and at the pinned commit in `cpp/gateway/conformance/oracle-revision.txt`. Read `cpp/gateway/README.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (driver: `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release|asan <test or --shard N/4>`) and `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (coroutine rules are mandatory). Your branch becomes a pull request; your final message is its body: a short plain-language summary for the owner.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; less first-party code is preferred; the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) must hold and security must never get weaker.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` or anything outside `cpp/gateway/` and `static/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


HARD WORKING RULE: your process can be restarted without warning and then knows only what is committed. One change per commit, tree building at every commit, report updated in the same commit. After a restart read your report and `git log` first.

OWNED PATHS
- `cpp/gateway/include/uos/rt/limits.hpp`, the call sites under `cpp/gateway/src/rt/**`, `cpp/gateway/src/runtime/**`, `cpp/gateway/src/auth/**` that hand untrusted bytes to a library, their tests, `cpp/gateway/docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md` (new), your report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-input-limits-20261119.md`.

TASK
`include/uos/rt/limits.hpp` declares the central input limits (HTTP header block 32 KiB, HTTP body 16 MiB, WebSocket message 16 MiB and 60 s idle, regex pattern 4 KiB / subject 1 MiB / 10 ms deadline, JSON 16 MiB / depth 128, CBOR 1 MiB / depth 8, certificate 64 KiB / chain 256 KiB, image-edit sizes). Hand-written parsers were recently replaced by libraries (llhttp, simdjson, Ada, QCBOR, OpenSSL ASN.1/X.509, QuickJS-ng libregexp, Boost.Beast, zlib, ICU). Establish, for EVERY boundary where bytes from a client, an upstream provider, or stored data reach one of those libraries, that a limit from this header is enforced BEFORE the library sees the input, and that exceeding it produces the gateway's normal error for that path (a 4xx for client input such as 413/431/400, an upstream error for provider input) rather than a crash, unbounded memory or unbounded CPU. Method: (1) inventory every call into each library (grep the wrappers) with the origin of its input (client, upstream, stored, trusted constant) in a table in `docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md`; (2) for each untrusted boundary, name the constant that bounds it and the test that proves it, or add the missing check and a test that sends limit and limit+1; (3) known gap to close: the regex engine's per-operation deadline is 2.5 seconds while the header says 10 ms: find every regex executed on untrusted subjects or patterns, measure the slowest legitimate one in the suite, and set the enforced deadline as low as the suite and the image/compaction fixtures allow (state the number and why if it cannot be 10 ms), making the header constant and the engine agree; (4) also bound decompression (gzip/brotli/zstd output size and ratio for upstream and client bodies), URL length, header count, multipart part count and size, WebSocket frame fragmentation, SSE line length from upstreams, and base64 decode sizes: add constants to `limits.hpp` where one is missing, choosing values that keep every existing test and the application's real needs (the application already has some smaller, more specific limits: keep the smaller one). Do not lower an existing limit that a legitimate request in the suite needs; do not raise any. No behaviour change for inputs within limits.
Verification: each new or tightened limit has a test at the boundary in release and under `--config asan`; then all four release shards and the sanitizer shards for runtime, HTTP, WebSocket, passkey, KV, regex and provider-stream tests; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check`. The hosted CI also runs when your branch is pushed.

DONE WHEN
`docs/SECURITY-LIMITS.md` lists every untrusted boundary with its limit, error and test; no boundary is unbounded; the regex deadline in the header is the one enforced; the checks pass.
